reviews.text: It's a terrible clinic!!! We waited in line for 7 hours and no one came to see us. I told them the dog was sick, but they didn't care!
Terrible

I don't question the doctors' professionalism, but I find there's little attention paid to explaining the medical decisions required (visits, tests, or therapies). Explaining the reasons would allow the pet owner, in need of care, to actively and informedly participate. Verbal exchange leads to mutual collaboration, with the owner's conviction that subjecting the animal to some stress is worthwhile.

We went to the emergency room at 1:00 a.m. with Jack and were lucky enough to find Dr. Maria Caterina. She helped us right away and was incredibly helpful and kind. She took care of Jack with such care and thoughtfulness, putting our minds at ease.
A truly kind and sweet person, we were so happy!
Jack, thank you ❤️🐶

Years later, I tried again... I arrived at 10 pm, half an hour out because they wouldn't open for us, and once inside, an hour before seeing anyone... Let's just say that years go by, but the places remain the same. Even the fact that you only find students working at night.

My dog ​​had parvovirus when he was a puppy. I took him to the clinic, and they were always available. They saved his life. They always called me to keep me updated. Then one time he fractured his foot, and he advised me to go to Anicura Veterinary Clinic (if I'm not mistaken) because they could perform that surgery. Top. Thanks.
Excellent experience with eye specialist Dr. Bonfanti. Professional and kind, she solved a very difficult corneal problem for my Dora.
Excellent clinic for our furry friends, the staff is attentive to every little need of our animals, they are always available to clarify any fears and questions that are raised by us.....

At the Gran Sasso Clinic, I found, in addition to their extraordinary professionalism, a rare humanity and empathy. I will never forget the hug from the veterinarian who greeted me as I carried away the body of my beloved Otis: a gesture that, in a moment of immense pain, made me feel understood and less alone. I will always be grateful to the entire facility for the care and love they gave my little one. ❤️

The best clinic in Milan for emergencies and other types of care.
They don't offer "money-eating" tests like the clinic I used to go to; the patient already has a clear picture (with a letter of introduction from the attending veterinarian 😅).

Furthermore, Dr. Camilla has proven herself to be competent, helpful, and interested on two occasions.
Both during the visit and during the patient's follow-up.

Trust me, they're excellent.

Excellent vets, despite the many emergencies and workload, they always manage to provide the best care possible and always with a smile. They saved my cat Gigi after a bad fall from the third floor. Special thanks to today's doctors, Dr. Gonzi, Grasso, and Amato, and to the receptionist who promptly brought my cat to their attention. Thanks to all the staff!

Unacceptable. You call for an emergency and have an eight-minute hold with that diabolical music blasting your ears, they answer and hang up.
I call back, wait 20 minutes, and they hang up after I express my disagreement with this behavior. Two years ago, when I called, they would immediately answer whether it was an emergency or not. And I needed to speak to someone urgently this evening, so I went to a different emergency room.

The Gran Sasso Clinic is truly a place of excellence, where professionalism and humanity meet. Our Camillo is cared for by Dr. Signorelli and the entire Cardiology staff, who take care of him with expertise, attention, and truly extraordinary availability. A heartfelt thank you to Dr. Signorelli and the entire department for the professionalism and humanity they demonstrate every day.
First the money, then maybe it will help you…

Unfortunately, it was a negative experience. The clinic gives off an extremely commercial feel, and it seems like they treat their clients primarily as cash machines. During the visit, Dr. Agnello assured us she would call us back within a few days to discuss the test results and agree on a treatment plan. She never called us back, and subsequently, it was impossible to get in touch with her, despite her having suggested we contact her again.
Each time, we were sent back to reception, where the only solution was to schedule a new general consultation, which, of course, required a fee.
In the end, we found another veterinarian who was competent, helpful, and reasonably priced. We definitely won't be returning to this clinic.
Thanks again to Dr. Consoli for having looked after Gigi for many years, guaranteeing him a great quality and long life (16) and for having put him to sleep with great sweetness this morning....

Good, but not great.

I would like to sincerely thank Dr. Giovanni Dalli Cardillo for the way he cared for my dog ​​during a series of epileptic seizures: a truly skilled, meticulous, and efficient veterinarian.

I must, however, make a negative comment about the receptionist.
My dog ​​was on a stretcher, in the midst of a post-ictal phase (due to the seizure), in a very, very noisy waiting room with other dogs. Despite my request to put him somewhere quieter to avoid stress while we waited, I was simply dismissed with a simple "you have to wait here." The result: he had another seizure right there in the waiting room. I remember that in dogs with these problems, auditory and visual stress are the worst enemy, as I also told the receptionist. Perhaps he should consult with someone competent to handle requests and assessments of extreme patients.

Maximum respect and gratitude to the doctor, but the management of emergencies at the entrance definitely needs improvement.

I'd give it 0 stars, but it's not possible!!
Terrible vet, really terrible! This is the second time I've taken my Sleepy, since it's close to home, but it's highly discouraged. The first time he had a swollen ear, and without examining him or anything else, they told me it wasn't "urgent" to take him elsewhere or schedule an appointment. The last straw was Monday, August 31st. I should point out that it's a 24-hour veterinary clinic, and I went urgently because my Sleepy was breathing heavily, his tongue was hanging out, and he couldn't stand up. I explained everything to the woman who opened the door, and what did she say? "That he couldn't be seen until 8:00 a.m. I replied, shocked, telling her that the situation was serious, and she told me I could
go elsewhere. I asked her where, and what did she say? That they had a clinic in Desio or Monza. Madness!!!!! I managed to take him to my trusted vet, which is further away, but I had to. My Sleepy died that same day. I really don't recommend this clinic; go elsewhere instead. The treatment they provide is truly terrible, and who knows what would have happened if I had decided to stay there and wait until 8:00 a.m. He wouldn't have even survived until the afternoon, given the proper care!!!

I learned about this wonderful clinic through word of mouth from a friend. My poodle needed cruciate ligament surgery. Previous consultations at other facilities had been a disaster, with more fears than certainties. Here, I found great professionalism and a peaceful environment, especially with regards to animals. A heartfelt thank you goes to Dr. Galardi and Dr. Zortea for helping me through all my fears until the end, and for the love they gave to Koko, who immediately felt safe. Koko underwent two TPLO surgeries, first on her right leg and then on her left leg. Everything went perfectly. The post-op explanation was excellent. I live 20 km from the clinic, but from today onwards, she will be my safe haven.

It took me eight months to write this review. I waited deliberately, because I didn't want to do it overwhelmed by the anger, pain, and resentment of those days.
On New Year's Eve, my dog ​​wasn't feeling well. She'd been recovering from about a week of diarrhea, which we were already treating, but that evening she was visibly different from usual. At 2:00 AM she vomited, a new symptom. At 5:00 AM she vomited again, and I noticed she'd urinated on herself, something she'd never seen before. I should point out that she wasn't afraid of fireworks.
At 5:30 AM we rushed to the Gran Sasso Veterinary Clinic. At the reception desk, we found two people who were visibly just awake, understandably so given the time of day and it being New Year's Eve, but also clearly annoyed and almost surprised that we'd shown up there. I felt out of place for bringing an animal in distress to what, however, presented itself as a 24-hour veterinary emergency room.
We were told that at that moment they were only treating hospitalized patients and that we should go home and show up again at 8:00.
Even today, I struggle to understand this. How can you send an animal who is clearly not well home at 5:30? Especially on New Year's Eve, one of those nights when an increase in emergencies is entirely predictable, both in human and veterinary emergency rooms.
We returned at 8:00. My dog ​​was examined by a doctor who, only later and through mutual acquaintances, I discovered was an anesthesiologist. An X-ray was performed, we were told it was gastritis, an anti-vomiting medication was administered, and we were advised to change her diet and take enzymes. Not even a blood sample was taken.
When I mentioned the urination incident, I was told that she was probably frightened by the fireworks. We pay hundreds of euros and return home without a real answer.
The next morning, I notice she's limping. I rush to the vet who was treating her, who was closed on New Year's Eve. Blood tests immediately reveal kidney failure. One leg is completely cold: she's had a blood clot.
They recommend a CT scan, either at Gran Sasso or at a clinic in Voghera. I choose to drive an extra hour rather than return to Gran Sasso.
The CT scan reveals a devastating truth: lung cancer with widespread metastases. Before those days, she hadn't shown any signs that would have led us to suspect such a situation.
She will pass away the next day.

I want to be very clear: I'm not saying the Gran Sasso Clinic is responsible for my dog's death. I don't need to find someone to blame for the loss of the love of my life.
What I question is the way we were treated. I can understand that it was New Year's Eve, she was tired, and that it's not always possible to get the correct diagnosis right away. However, I cannot understand a 24-hour emergency room sending a pet home at 5:30 a.m. and then, just hours later, dismissing such a situation without even a blood test.
Tests that the next day immediately revealed kidney failure.
Finding out later that the doctor was an anesthesiologist doesn't diminish that specialty, but it does make me wonder if my dog ​​received the thorough clinical care I would have expected from an emergency room.
I can't know if doing more research sooner would have changed the outcome. Probably not. But it would have made a huge difference in how we handled her last day: we would have known the situation was serious and wouldn't have wasted hours believing we'd have to wait at home.
It wasn't my first negative experience with this clinic either: on the few previous occasions, I'd already experienced interminable waits accompanied by the promise that we'd be called "soon."
I waited eight months to report the facts with a clear head. And even after eight months, for me, what happened remains scandalous.
